1	"""User-feedback diagnosis over one Session-bound OpenSpec graph."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import json
6	import re
7	from importlib import resources
8	from typing import Any
9	
10	from ccwhat.analyzer import AnalysisError, run_mc_analysis
11	
12	
13	MAX_GRAPH_CONTEXT_CHARS = 28_000
14	MAX_TEXT_PREVIEW = 700
15	MAX_TOOL_INPUT_PREVIEW = 900
16	
17	
18	def analyze_graph_feedback(
19	    *,
20	    feedback: str,
21	    action_graph: dict[str, Any],
22	    event_graph: dict[str, Any],
23	    analyzer_cmd: list[str] | tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
24	    analyzer_agent: str | None = None,
25	    analyzer_timeout: int | float | None = None,
26	    runner: Any | None = None,
27	) -> dict[str, Any]:
28	    """Run one local Analyzer CLI session and return validated graph references."""
29	    prompt = build_graph_attribution_prompt(feedback, action_graph, event_graph)
30	    try:
31	        raw, elapsed_ms = run_mc_analysis(
32	            prompt,
33	            cmd=analyzer_cmd,
34	            agent=analyzer_agent,
35	            timeout=analyzer_timeout,
36	            runner=runner,
37	        )
38	    except AnalysisError as exc:
39	        return _unavailable_result(exc.code, exc.message)
40	
41	    try:
42	        parsed = parse_graph_attribution_output(raw)
43	    except ValueError as exc:
44	        return _unavailable_result("invalid_analyzer_json", str(exc))
45	
46	    result = validate_graph_attribution_result(parsed, action_graph, event_graph)
47	    result["elapsed_ms"] = elapsed_ms
48	    result["analyzer_agent"] = analyzer_agent or "claude"
49	    return result
50	
51	
52	def build_graph_attribution_prompt(
53	    feedback: str,
54	    action_graph: dict[str, Any],
55	    event_graph: dict[str, Any],
56	) -> str:
57	    template = resources.files("ccwhat").joinpath("assets/graph_attribution_prompt.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
58	    context = build_compact_graph_context(action_graph, event_graph)
59	    return template.replace("{{feedback}}", feedback.strip()).replace("{{graph_context}}", context)
60	
61	
62	def build_compact_graph_context(
63	    action_graph: dict[str, Any],
64	    event_graph: dict[str, Any],
65	) -> str:
66	    actions = [item for item in action_graph.get("actions", []) if isinstance(item, dict)]
67	    nodes = [item for item in event_graph.get("nodes", []) if isinstance(item, dict)]
68	
69	    ranked = sorted(enumerate(nodes), key=lambda item: (-_event_priority(item[1]), item[0]))
70	    selected_indexes: set[int] = set()
71	    used = 0
72	    compact_by_index: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
73	    for index, node in ranked:
74	        compact = _compact_event(node)
75	        size = len(json.dumps(compact, ensure_ascii=False))
76	        if used + size > MAX_GRAPH_CONTEXT_CHARS and selected_indexes:
77	            continue
78	        selected_indexes.add(index)
79	        compact_by_index[index] = compact
80	        used += size
81	
82	    selected_events = [compact_by_index[index] for index in sorted(selected_indexes)]
83	    selected_ids = {str(item.get("event_id") or "") for item in selected_events}
84	    compact_actions = []
85	    for action in actions:
86	        event_ids = [str(value) for value in action.get("event_ids", []) if str(value) in selected_ids]
87	        compact_actions.append({
88	            "action_id": action.get("action_id"),
89	            "type": action.get("type"),
90	            "status": action.get("status"),
91	            "event_ids": event_ids,
92	            "mapping_reasons": [
93	                item.get("reason")
94	                for item in action.get("evidence", [])
95	                if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("reason")
96	            ][:12],
97	        })
98	
99	    return json.dumps(
100	        {
101	            "actions": compact_actions,
102	            "events": selected_events,
103	            "omitted_event_count": max(0, len(nodes) - len(selected_events)),
104	            "source_note": "Claude Code raw Session behavior; final repository state is not verified",
105	        },
106	        ensure_ascii=False,
107	        indent=2,
108	    )
109	
110	
111	def parse_graph_attribution_output(raw: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
112	    text = str(raw or "").strip()
113	    if not text:
114	        raise ValueError("Analyzer returned empty diagnosis output.")
115	
116	    fenced = re.search(r"```(?:json)?\s*(\{.*?\})\s*```", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
117	    candidate = fenced.group(1) if fenced else text
118	    try:
119	        value = json.loads(candidate)
120	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
121	        start = candidate.find("{")
122	        if start < 0:
123	            raise ValueError("Analyzer output does not contain a JSON object.") from None
124	        try:
125	            value, _ = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(candidate[start:])
126	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
127	            raise ValueError(f"Analyzer output is not valid diagnosis JSON: {exc.msg}.") from exc
128	    if not isinstance(value, dict):
129	        raise ValueError("Analyzer diagnosis JSON must be an object.")
130	    return value
131	
132	
133	def validate_graph_attribution_result(
134	    value: dict[str, Any],
135	    action_graph: dict[str, Any],
136	    event_graph: dict[str, Any],
137	) -> dict[str, Any]:
138	    actions = {
139	        str(item.get("action_id")): item
140	        for item in action_graph.get("actions", [])
141	        if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("action_id")
142	    }
143	    events = {
144	        str(item.get("node_id")): item
145	        for item in event_graph.get("nodes", [])
146	        if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("node_id")
147	    }
148	    event_actions: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
149	    for action_id, action in actions.items():
150	        for event_id in action.get("event_ids", []):
151	            event_actions.setdefault(str(event_id), []).append(action_id)
152	
153	    missing = _string_list(value.get("missing_evidence"))
154	    suspicious_actions = []
155	    seen_actions: set[str] = set()
156	    for item in _dict_list(value.get("suspicious_actions")):
157	        action_id = str(item.get("action_id") or "")
158	        if action_id not in actions:
159	            if action_id:
160	                missing.append(f"Analyzer referenced unknown Action ID: {action_id}")
161	            continue
162	        if action_id in seen_actions:
163	            continue
164	        seen_actions.add(action_id)
165	        suspicious_actions.append({
166	            "action_id": action_id,
167	            "reason": _clip(item.get("reason"), MAX_TEXT_PREVIEW),
168	        })
169	
170	    suspicious_events = []
171	    seen_events: set[str] = set()
172	    for item in _dict_list(value.get("suspicious_events")):
173	        event_id = str(item.get("event_id") or "")
174	        if event_id not in events:
175	            if event_id:
176	                missing.append(f"Analyzer referenced unknown Event ID: {event_id}")
177	            continue
178	        if event_id in seen_events:
179	            continue
180	        seen_events.add(event_id)
181	        requested_action = str(item.get("action_id") or "")
182	        actual_actions = event_actions.get(event_id, [])
183	        adjusted = False
184	        if actual_actions and requested_action not in actual_actions:
185	            requested_action = actual_actions[0]
186	            adjusted = True
187	        elif requested_action not in actions:
188	            requested_action = actual_actions[0] if actual_actions else ""
189	            adjusted = bool(actual_actions)
190	        row = {
191	            "event_id": event_id,
192	            "action_id": requested_action or None,
193	            "reason": _clip(item.get("reason"), MAX_TEXT_PREVIEW),
194	        }
195	        if adjusted:
196	            row["mapping_adjusted"] = True
197	        suspicious_events.append(row)
198	
199	    symptoms = []
200	    for item in _dict_list(value.get("symptoms"))[:6]:
201	        symptoms.append({
202	            "type": _clip(item.get("type"), 80) or "unknown",
203	            "summary": _clip(item.get("summary"), MAX_TEXT_PREVIEW),
204	        })
205	
206	    status = "complete" if suspicious_actions or suspicious_events else "insufficient_evidence"
207	    if status == "insufficient_evidence":
208	        missing.append("Analyzer did not return any valid Action or Event references.")
209	    return {
210	        "available": True,
211	        "status": status,
212	        "symptoms": symptoms,
213	        "suspicious_actions": suspicious_actions,
214	        "suspicious_events": suspicious_events,
215	        "missing_evidence": _dedupe(missing),
216	        "summary": _clip(value.get("summary"), 2000) or "No diagnosis summary was returned.",
217	    }
218	
219	
220	def _compact_event(node: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
221	    data = node.get("data") if isinstance(node.get("data"), dict) else {}
222	    tool_input = data.get("tool_input")
223	    return {
224	        "event_id": node.get("node_id"),
225	        "type": node.get("type"),
226	        "label": _clip(node.get("label"), 240),
227	        "timestamp": node.get("timestamp"),
228	        "agent_id": node.get("agent_id"),
229	        "turn_index": data.get("turn_index"),
230	        "tool_name": data.get("tool_name"),
231	        "tool_call_id": data.get("tool_call_id") or data.get("tool_use_id"),
232	        "files": list(data.get("files") or [])[:20],
233	        "command": _clip(data.get("command"), MAX_TEXT_PREVIEW),
234	        "text": _clip(data.get("text"), MAX_TEXT_PREVIEW),
235	        "tool_input": _clip_json(tool_input, MAX_TOOL_INPUT_PREVIEW),
236	        "result_summary": _clip(data.get("result_summary"), MAX_TEXT_PREVIEW),
237	        "is_error": bool(data.get("is_error")),
238	    }
239	
240	
241	def _event_priority(node: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
242	    node_type = str(node.get("type") or "")
243	    data = node.get("data") if isinstance(node.get("data"), dict) else {}
244	    if data.get("is_error") or node_type == "error":
245	        return 100
246	    return {
247	        "file_edit": 90,
248	        "command": 85,
249	        "final_claim": 80,
250	        "tool_result": 75,
251	        "user_message": 70,
252	        "file_read": 45,
253	        "assistant_text": 35,
254	    }.get(node_type, 30)
255	
256	
257	def _unavailable_result(code: str, message: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
258	    return {
259	        "available": False,
260	        "status": "unavailable",
261	        "code": code,
262	        "symptoms": [],
263	        "suspicious_actions": [],
264	        "suspicious_events": [],
265	        "missing_evidence": [message],
266	        "summary": "Feedback diagnosis is unavailable.",
267	    }
268	
269	
270	def _dict_list(value: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:

1	## Why
2	
3	现有 OpenSpec Graph 已能从 Claude Code Session 生成固定七节点 Action Graph 和 step-level Event Graph，但产品尚未形成“用户描述问题 -> 定位可疑 Action -> 定位具体 Event -> 输出可回看证据的报告”闭环。
4	
5	原有 change 计划继续扩展 Action/Event 规则打分，但这会在 MVP 阶段引入大量无法校准的权重和因果假设。当前最需要验证的是：仅使用一个 OpenSpec change 对应的一份 Claude Code 原始 Session，复用项目现有 Analyzer Adapter 启动一次本地 AI CLI 非交互分析，是否已经能给用户提供有价值的粗到细诊断。
6	
7	## What Changes
8	
9	- 保留固定 OpenSpec 七节点 Action Graph，只把状态收敛为 `observed|not_observed|failed`，不再使用流程距离产生根因分数。
10	- 加固基于 Claude Code 原始 Session 的 Event Graph：唯一 Event ID、Tool Call/Result 配对、文件/命令/错误/result summary 和 raw reference。
11	- 修正 Event 到 Action 的最小映射规则，保留映射理由，未映射 Event 不丢失。
12	- 新增用户反馈归因入口：输入 `session_id`、`change` 和自然语言 feedback。
13	- 复用 `run_mc_analysis()` 和 Analyzer Registry，启动一次本地 Claude/Codex/OpenCode CLI 非交互会话；不新增模型 API Client 或 API Key 配置。
14	- Analyzer 输出严格结构化诊断，程序校验所有 Action/Event 引用并删除编造 ID。
15	- Viewer 增加反馈输入、诊断报告，以及从报告定位粗图 Action 和细图 Event 的交互。
16	- 提供一个真实结构的 OpenSpec 驱动 Claude Code Session mock，用于前端手动验收。
17	
18	## Non-Goals
19	
20	- 不接 Runtime Task、Task Dataset、Dataset export 或 `task.diff`。
21	- 不支持一个 Session 中包含多个 OpenSpec change。
22	- 不引入 Action Contract、Action Run、多模板适配器或 Artifact/Requirement/Outcome 图。
23	- 不实现复杂因果边、反事实执行、规则投票或数值 root-cause score。
24	- 不调用模型 HTTP API；本 change 只复用用户本机已安装并已登录的 AI CLI。
25	- 不让 Analyzer 修改代码或自动修复问题。
26

38	- **AND** Tool Calls and Tool Results SHALL be linked by stable Tool Call ID when available
39	
40	#### Scenario: Retain unmapped Events
41	- **WHEN** an Event cannot map to a fixed OpenSpec Action
42	- **THEN** the Event SHALL remain in the Event Graph
43	- **AND** its Action mapping SHALL be absent rather than represented by a fabricated required Action
44	
45	### Requirement: User feedback diagnosis through Analyzer Adapter
46	
47	系统 SHALL analyze natural-language feedback through the existing local Analyzer Adapter.
48	
49	#### Scenario: Start one non-interactive analyzer session
50	- **WHEN** the user submits feedback for a loaded Session/change graph
51	- **THEN** the system SHALL build a compact Action/Event context
52	- **AND** SHALL call `run_mc_analysis()` once using the configured local AI CLI protocol
53	- **AND** SHALL NOT require a model HTTP API or project-level API Key configuration
54	
55	#### Scenario: Analyzer unavailable
56	- **WHEN** the local analyzer CLI is missing, unauthenticated, fails, or times out
57	- **THEN** the API SHALL return a structured unavailable/error status
58	- **AND** the Viewer SHALL show a readable message without fabricating suspicious Events
59	
60	### Requirement: Validated structured diagnosis
61	
62	系统 SHALL validate all Analyzer-produced graph references before returning a diagnosis.
63	
64	#### Scenario: Valid diagnosis references
65	- **WHEN** Analyzer output contains suspicious Action and Event IDs
66	- **THEN** every returned Action ID SHALL exist in the fixed Action Graph
67	- **AND** every returned Event ID SHALL exist in the current Event Graph
68	- **AND** invalid or fabricated IDs SHALL NOT be returned as valid evidence
69	
70	#### Scenario: Invalid Analyzer JSON
71	- **WHEN** Analyzer output is empty, malformed, or cannot be parsed as the diagnosis schema
72	- **THEN** diagnosis SHALL return a parse/error status with missing evidence
73	- **AND** SHALL NOT invent fallback root-cause references
74	
75	### Requirement: Viewer feedback-to-report flow
76	
77	Diagnostics Viewer SHALL provide an end-to-end feedback diagnosis flow.
78	
79	#### Scenario: Submit feedback and inspect report
80	- **WHEN** the user loads a Session-bound OpenSpec graph and submits feedback
81	- **THEN** Viewer SHALL display the diagnosis summary, suspicious Actions, suspicious Events, and missing evidence
82	- **AND** the user SHALL be able to locate or highlight referenced Action and Event nodes
83	
84	### Requirement: Realistic OpenSpec Session fixture
85	
86	系统 SHALL include a realistic Claude Code Session mock for manual MVP acceptance.
87	
88	#### Scenario: Diagnose the mock Session
89	- **WHEN** Viewer loads the mock Session and its OpenSpec change
90	- **THEN** it SHALL display fixed Action and step-level Event graphs
91	- **AND** manually submitted feedback SHALL produce a report referencing real Action/Event IDs from the mock graph

43	   - Progress (total, complete, remaining)
44	   - Task list with status
45	   - Dynamic instruction based on current state
46	
47	   **Handle states:**
48	   - If `state: "blocked"` (missing artifacts): show message, suggest using openspec-continue-change
49	   - If `state: "all_done"`: congratulate, suggest archive
50	   - Otherwise: proceed to implementation
51	
52	4. **Read context files**
53	
54	   Read every file path listed under `contextFiles` from the apply instructions output.
55	   The files depend on the schema being used:
56	   - **spec-driven**: proposal, specs, design, tasks
57	   - Other schemas: follow the contextFiles from CLI output
58	
59	5. **Show current progress**
60	
61	   Display:
62	   - Schema being used
63	   - Progress: "N/M tasks complete"
64	   - Remaining tasks overview
65	   - Dynamic instruction from CLI
66	
67	6. **Implement tasks (loop until done or blocked)**
68	
69	   For each pending task:
70	   - Show which task is being worked on
71	   - Make the code changes required
72	   - Keep changes minimal and focused
73	   - Mark task complete in the tasks file: `- [ ]` → `- [x]`
74	   - Sync the OpenSpec graph after marking the task complete:
75	     ```bash
76	     ccwhat openspec-graph sync --change "<name>" --event task_completed --task "<task description>"
77	     ```
78	   - Continue to next task
79

81	   - Task is unclear → ask for clarification
82	   - Implementation reveals a design issue → suggest updating artifacts
83	   - Error or blocker encountered → report and wait for guidance
84	   - User interrupts

88	   Display:
89	   - Tasks completed this session
90	   - Overall progress: "N/M tasks complete"
91	   - If all done: suggest archive
92	   - If paused: explain why and wait for guidance
93	   - If validation is run, record it:
94	     ```bash
95	     ccwhat openspec-graph sync --change "<name>" --event validate_ran --success
96	     ```
97	     Use `--failure` instead of `--success` when validation fails.
98	
99	**Output During Implementation**
100	
101	```
102	## Implementing: <change-name> (schema: <schema-name>)
103	
104	Working on task 3/7: <task description>
105	[...implementation happening...]
106	✓ Task complete
107	
108	Working on task 4/7: <task description>
109	[...implementation happening...]
110	✓ Task complete
111	```
112

117	
118	**Change:** <change-name>
119	**Schema:** <schema-name>
120	**Progress:** 7/7 tasks complete ✓
121	
122	### Completed This Session
123	- [x] Task 1
124	- [x] Task 2
125	...
126	
127	All tasks complete! Ready to archive this change.
128	```
129	
130	**Output On Pause (Issue Encountered)**
131	
132	```
133	## Implementation Paused
134	
135	**Change:** <change-name>
136	**Schema:** <schema-name>
137	**Progress:** 4/7 tasks complete
138	
139	### Issue Encountered
140	<description of the issue>
141	
142	**Options:**
143	1. <option 1>
144	2. <option 2>
145	3. Other approach
146	
147	What would you like to do?
148	```
149	
150	**Guardrails**
151	- Keep going through tasks until done or blocked
152	- Always read context files before starting (from the apply instructions output)
153	- If task is ambiguous, pause and ask before implementing
154	- If implementation reveals issues, pause and suggest artifact updates
155	- Keep code changes minimal and scoped to each task
156	- Update task checkbox immediately after completing each task
157	- Keep `openspec/changes/<name>/graph/` synchronized after every completed task and validation run
158	- Pause on errors, blockers, or unclear requirements - don't guess
159	- Use contextFiles from CLI output, don't assume specific file names
160	
161	**Fluid Workflow Integration**
162	
163	This skill supports the "actions on a change" model:
164	
165	- **Can be invoked anytime**: Before all artifacts are done (if tasks exist), after partial implementation, interleaved with other actions
166	- **Allows artifact updates**: If implementation reveals design issues, suggest updating artifacts - not phase-locked, work fluidly

1	---
2	name: openspec-explore
3	description: Enter explore mode - a thinking partner for exploring ideas, investigating problems, and clarifying requirements. Use when the user wants to think through something before or during a change.
4	license: MIT
5	compatibility: Requires openspec CLI.
6	metadata:
7	  author: openspec
8	  version: "1.0"
9	  generatedBy: "1.3.1"
10	---
11	
12	Enter explore mode. Think deeply. Visualize freely. Follow the conversation wherever it goes.
13	
14	**IMPORTANT: Explore mode is for thinking, not implementing.** You may read files, search code, and investigate the codebase, but you must NEVER write code or implement features. If the user asks you to implement something, remind them to exit explore mode first and create a change proposal. You MAY create OpenSpec artifacts (proposals, designs, specs) if the user asks—that's capturing thinking, not implementing.
15	
16	**This is a stance, not a workflow.** There are no fixed steps, no required sequence, no mandatory outputs. You're a thinking partner helping the user explore.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## The Stance
21	
22	- **Curious, not prescriptive** - Ask questions that emerge naturally, don't follow a script
23	- **Open threads, not interrogations** - Surface multiple interesting directions and let the user follow what resonates. Don't funnel them through a single path of questions.
24	- **Visual** - Use ASCII diagrams liberally when they'd help clarify thinking
25	- **Adaptive** - Follow interesting threads, pivot when new information emerges
26	- **Patient** - Don't rush to conclusions, let the shape of the problem emerge
27	- **Grounded** - Explore the actual codebase when relevant, don't just theorize
28	
29	---
30	
31	## What You Might Do
32	
33	Depending on what the user brings, you might:
34	
35	**Explore the problem space**
36	- Ask clarifying questions that emerge from what they said
37	- Challenge assumptions
38	- Reframe the problem
39	- Find analogies
40	
41	**Investigate the codebase**
42	- Map existing architecture relevant to the discussion
43	- Find integration points
44	- Identify patterns already in use
45	- Surface hidden complexity
46	
47	**Compare options**
48	- Brainstorm multiple approaches
49	- Build comparison tables
50	- Sketch tradeoffs
51	- Recommend a path (if asked)
52	
53	**Visualize**
54	```
55	┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
56	│     Use ASCII diagrams liberally        │
57	├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
58	│                                         │
59	│      ┌────────┐         ┌────────┐      │
60	│      │ State  │────────▶│ State  │      │
61	│      │   A    │         │   B    │      │
62	│      └────────┘         └────────┘      │
63	│                                         │
64	│   System diagrams, state machines,      │
65	│   data flows, architecture sketches,    │
66	│   dependency graphs, comparison tables  │
67	│                                         │
68	└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
69	```
70	
71	**Surface risks and unknowns**
72	- Identify what could go wrong
73	- Find gaps in understanding
74	- Suggest spikes or investigations
75	
76	---
77	
78	## OpenSpec Awareness
79	
80	You have full context of the OpenSpec system. Use it naturally, don't force it.
81	
82	### Check for context
83	
84	At the start, quickly check what exists:
85	```bash
86	openspec list --json
87	```
88	
89	This tells you:
90	- If there are active changes
91	- Their names, schemas, and status
92	- What the user might be working on
93	
94	### When no change exists
95	
96	Think freely. When insights crystallize, you might offer:
97	
98	- "This feels solid enough to start a change. Want me to create a proposal?"
99	- Or keep exploring - no pressure to formalize
100	
101	### When a change exists
102	
103	If the user mentions a change or you detect one is relevant:
104	
105	1. **Read existing artifacts for context**
106	   - `openspec/changes/<name>/proposal.md`
107	   - `openspec/changes/<name>/design.md`
108	   - `openspec/changes/<name>/tasks.md`
109	   - etc.
110	
111	2. **Reference them naturally in conversation**
112	   - "Your design mentions using Redis, but we just realized SQLite fits better..."
113	   - "The proposal scopes this to premium users, but we're now thinking everyone..."
114	
115	3. **Offer to capture when decisions are made**
116	
117	    | Insight Type               | Where to Capture               |
118	    |----------------------------|--------------------------------|
119	    | New requirement discovered | `specs/<capability>/spec.md` |
120	    | Requirement changed        | `specs/<capability>/spec.md` |
121	    | Design decision made       | `design.md`                  |
122	    | Scope changed              | `proposal.md`                |
123	    | New work identified        | `tasks.md`                   |
124	    | Assumption invalidated     | Relevant artifact              |
125	
126	   Example offers:
127	   - "That's a design decision. Capture it in design.md?"
128	   - "This is a new requirement. Add it to specs?"
129	   - "This changes scope. Update the proposal?"
130	
131	4. **The user decides** - Offer and move on. Don't pressure. Don't auto-capture.
132	
133	---
134	
135	## What You Don't Have To Do
136	
137	- Follow a script
138	- Ask the same questions every time
139	- Produce a specific artifact
140	- Reach a conclusion
141	- Stay on topic if a tangent is valuable
142	- Be brief (this is thinking time)
143	
144	---
145	
146	## Handling Different Entry Points
147	
148	**User brings a vague idea:**
149	```
150	User: I'm thinking about adding real-time collaboration
151	
152	You: Real-time collab is a big space. Let me think about this...
153	
154	      COLLABORATION SPECTRUM
155	      ════════════════════════════════════════════
156	
157	      Awareness          Coordination         Sync
158	          │                   │                 │
159	          ▼                   ▼                 ▼
160	      ┌────────┐         ┌────────┐        ┌────────┐
161	      │Presence│         │Cursors │        │  CRDT  │
162	      │  "3    │         │ Multi  │        │Conflict│
163	      │online" │         │ select │        │  free  │
164	      └────────┘         └────────┘        └────────┘
165	          │                   │                 │
166	       trivial            moderate           complex
167	
168	      Where's your head at?
169	```
170	
171	**User brings a specific problem:**
172	```
173	User: The auth system is a mess
174	
175	You: [reads codebase]
176	
177	     ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
178	     │              CURRENT AUTH FLOW              │
179	     └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
180	                        │
181	          ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
182	          ▼             ▼             ▼
183	     ┌─────────┐  ┌─────────┐  ┌─────────┐
184	     │ Google  │  │  GitHub │  │  Email  │
185	     │  OAuth  │  │  OAuth  │  │  Magic  │
186	     └────┬────┘  └────┬────┘  └────┬────┘
187	          │             │             │
188	          └─────────────┼─────────────┘
189	                        ▼
190	                  ┌───────────┐
191	                  │  Session  │
192	                  └─────┬─────┘
193	                        │
194	                        ▼
195	                  ┌───────────┐
196	                  │   Perms   │
197	                  └───────────┘
198	
199	     I see three tangles. Which one's burning?
200	```
201	
202	**User is stuck mid-implementation:**
203	```
204	User: /opsx:explore add-auth-system
205	      The OAuth integration is more complex than expected
206	
207	You: [reads change artifacts]
208	
209	     You're on task 4: "Implement OAuth flow"
210	
211	     Let me trace what's involved...
212	
213	     [draws diagram, explores options, suggests paths]
214	
215	     Want to update the design to reflect this?
216	     Or add a spike task to investigate?
217	```
218	
219	**User wants to compare options:**
220	```
221	User: Should we use Postgres or SQLite?
222	
223	You: Generic answer is boring. What's the context?
224	
225	User: A CLI tool that tracks local dev environments
226	
227	You: That changes everything.
228	
229	     ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
230	     │          CLI TOOL DATA STORAGE                  │
231	     └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
232	
233	     Key constraints:
234	     • No daemon running
235	     • Must work offline
236	     • Single user
237	
238	                  SQLite          Postgres
239	     Deployment   embedded ✓      needs server ✗
240	     Offline      yes ✓           no ✗
241	     Single file  yes ✓           no ✗
242	
243	     SQLite. Not even close.
244	
245	     Unless... is there a sync component?
246	```
247	
248	---
249	
250	## Ending Discovery
251	
252	There's no required ending. Discovery might:
253	
254	- **Flow into a proposal**: "Ready to start? I can create a change proposal."
255	- **Result in artifact updates**: "Updated design.md with these decisions"
256	- **Just provide clarity**: User has what they need, moves on
257	- **Continue later**: "We can pick this up anytime"
258	
259	When it feels like things are crystallizing, you might summarize:
260	
261	```
262	## What We Figured Out
263	
264	**The problem**: [crystallized understanding]
265	
266	**The approach**: [if one emerged]
267	
268	**Open questions**: [if any remain]
269	
270	**Next steps** (if ready):
271	- Create a change proposal
272	- Keep exploring: just keep talking
273	```
274	
275	But this summary is optional. Sometimes the thinking IS the value.
276	
277	---
278	
279	## Guardrails
280	
281	- **Don't implement** - Never write code or implement features. Creating OpenSpec artifacts is fine, writing application code is not.
282	- **Don't fake understanding** - If something is unclear, dig deeper
283	- **Don't rush** - Discovery is thinking time, not task time
284	- **Don't force structure** - Let patterns emerge naturally
285	- **Don't auto-capture** - Offer to save insights, don't just do it
286	- **Do visualize** - A good diagram is worth many paragraphs
287	- **Do explore the codebase** - Ground discussions in reality
288	- **Do question assumptions** - Including the user's and your own

74	git log --oneline -10 2>/dev/null || echo "No git history"
75	# Windows (PowerShell)
76	# git log --oneline -10 2>$null; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { echo "No git history" }
77	```
78	
79	### Present Suggestions
80	
81	From your analysis, present 3-4 specific suggestions:
82	
83	```
84	## Task Suggestions
85	
86	Based on scanning your codebase, here are some good starter tasks:
87	
88	**1. [Most promising task]**
89	   Location: `src/path/to/file.ts:42`
90	   Scope: ~1-2 files, ~20-30 lines
91	   Why it's good: [brief reason]
92	
93	**2. [Second task]**
94	   Location: `src/another/file.ts`
95	   Scope: ~1 file, ~15 lines
96	   Why it's good: [brief reason]
97	
98	**3. [Third task]**
99	   Location: [location]
100	   Scope: [estimate]
101	   Why it's good: [brief reason]
102	
103	**4. Something else?**
104	   Tell me what you'd like to work on.
105	
106	Which task interests you? (Pick a number or describe your own)
107	```
108	
109	**If nothing found:** Fall back to asking what the user wants to build:
110	> I didn't find obvious quick wins in your codebase. What's something small you've been meaning to add or fix?
111	
112	### Scope Guardrail
113	
114	If the user picks or describes something too large (major feature, multi-day work):
115	
116	```
117	That's a valuable task, but it's probably larger than ideal for your first OpenSpec run-through.
118	
119	For learning the workflow, smaller is better—it lets you see the full cycle without getting stuck in implementation details.
120	
121	**Options:**
122	1. **Slice it smaller** - What's the smallest useful piece of [their task]? Maybe just [specific slice]?
123	2. **Pick something else** - One of the other suggestions, or a different small task?
124	3. **Do it anyway** - If you really want to tackle this, we can. Just know it'll take longer.
125	
126	What would you prefer?
127	```
128	
129	Let the user override if they insist—this is a soft guardrail.
130	
131	---
132	
133	## Phase 3: Explore Demo
134	
135	Once a task is selected, briefly demonstrate explore mode:
136	
137	```
138	Before we create a change, let me quickly show you **explore mode**—it's how you think through problems before committing to a direction.
139	```
140	
141	Spend 1-2 minutes investigating the relevant code:
142	- Read the file(s) involved
143	- Draw a quick ASCII diagram if it helps
144	- Note any considerations
145	
146	```
147	## Quick Exploration
148	
149	[Your brief analysis—what you found, any considerations]
150	
151	┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
152	│   [Optional: ASCII diagram if helpful]  │
153	└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
154	
155	Explore mode (`/opsx:explore`) is for this kind of thinking—investigating before implementing. You can use it anytime you need to think through a problem.
156	
157	Now let's create a change to hold our work.
158	```
159	
160	**PAUSE** - Wait for user acknowledgment before proceeding.
161	
162	---
163	
164	## Phase 4: Create the Change
165	
166	**EXPLAIN:**
167	```
168	## Creating a Change
169	
170	A "change" in OpenSpec is a container for all the thinking and planning around a piece of work. It lives in `openspec/changes/<name>/` and holds your artifacts—proposal, specs, design, tasks.
171	
172	Let me create one for our task.
173	```
174	
175	**DO:** Create the change with a derived kebab-case name:
176	```bash
177	openspec new change "<derived-name>"
178	```
179	
180	**SHOW:**
181	```
182	Created: `openspec/changes/<name>/`
183	
184	The folder structure:
185	```
186	openspec/changes/<name>/
187	├── proposal.md    ← Why we're doing this (empty, we'll fill it)
188	├── design.md      ← How we'll build it (empty)
189	├── specs/         ← Detailed requirements (empty)
190	└── tasks.md       ← Implementation checklist (empty)
191	```
192	
193	Now let's fill in the first artifact—the proposal.
194	```
195	
196	---
197	
198	## Phase 5: Proposal
199	
200	**EXPLAIN:**
201	```
202	## The Proposal
203	
204	The proposal captures **why** we're making this change and **what** it involves at a high level. It's the "elevator pitch" for the work.
205	
206	I'll draft one based on our task.
207	```
208	
209	**DO:** Draft the proposal content (don't save yet):
210	
211	```
212	Here's a draft proposal:
213	
214	---
215	
216	## Why
217	
218	[1-2 sentences explaining the problem/opportunity]
219	
220	## What Changes
221	
222	[Bullet points of what will be different]
223	
224	## Capabilities
225	
226	### New Capabilities
227	- `<capability-name>`: [brief description]
228	
229	### Modified Capabilities
230	<!-- If modifying existing behavior -->
231	
232	## Impact
233	
234	- `src/path/to/file.ts`: [what changes]
235	- [other files if applicable]
236	
237	---
238	
239	Does this capture the intent? I can adjust before we save it.
240	```
241	
242	**PAUSE** - Wait for user approval/feedback.
243	
244	After approval, save the proposal:
245	```bash
246	openspec instructions proposal --change "<name>" --json
247	```
248	Then write the content to `openspec/changes/<name>/proposal.md`.
249	
250	```
251	Proposal saved. This is your "why" document—you can always come back and refine it as understanding evolves.
252	
253	Next up: specs.
254	```
255	
256	---
257	
258	## Phase 6: Specs
259	
260	**EXPLAIN:**
261	```
262	## Specs
263	
264	Specs define **what** we're building in precise, testable terms. They use a requirement/scenario format that makes expected behavior crystal clear.
265	
266	For a small task like this, we might only need one spec file.
267	```
268	
269	**DO:** Create the spec file:
270	```bash
271	# Unix/macOS
272	mkdir -p openspec/changes/<name>/specs/<capability-name>
273	# Windows (PowerShell)
274	# New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "openspec/changes/<name>/specs/<capability-name>"
275	```
276	
277	Draft the spec content:
278	
279	```
280	Here's the spec:
281	
282	---
283	
284	## ADDED Requirements
285	
286	### Requirement: <Name>
287	
288	<Description of what the system should do>
289	
290	#### Scenario: <Scenario name>
291	
292	- **WHEN** <trigger condition>
293	- **THEN** <expected outcome>
294	- **AND** <additional outcome if needed>
295	
296	---
297	
298	This format—WHEN/THEN/AND—makes requirements testable. You can literally read them as test cases.
299	```
300	
301	Save to `openspec/changes/<name>/specs/<capability>/spec.md`.
302	
303	---
304	
305	## Phase 7: Design
306	
307	**EXPLAIN:**
308	```
309	## Design
310	
311	The design captures **how** we'll build it—technical decisions, tradeoffs, approach.
312	
313	For small changes, this might be brief. That's fine—not every change needs deep design discussion.
314	```
315	
316	**DO:** Draft design.md:
317	
318	```
319	Here's the design:
320	
321	---
322	
323	## Context
324	
325	[Brief context about the current state]
326	
327	## Goals / Non-Goals
328	
329	**Goals:**
330	- [What we're trying to achieve]
331	
332	**Non-Goals:**
333	- [What's explicitly out of scope]
334	
335	## Decisions
336	
337	### Decision 1: [Key decision]
338	
339	[Explanation of approach and rationale]
340	
341	---
342	
343	For a small task, this captures the key decisions without over-engineering.
344	```
345	
346	Save to `openspec/changes/<name>/design.md`.
347	
348	---
349	
350	## Phase 8: Tasks
351	
352	**EXPLAIN:**
353	```
354	## Tasks
355	
356	Finally, we break the work into implementation tasks—checkboxes that drive the apply phase.
357	
358	These should be small, clear, and in logical order.
359	```
360	
361	**DO:** Generate tasks based on specs and design:
362	
363	```
364	Here are the implementation tasks:
365	
366	---
367	
368	## 1. [Category or file]
369	
370	- [ ] 1.1 [Specific task]
371	- [ ] 1.2 [Specific task]
372	
373	## 2. Verify
374	
375	- [ ] 2.1 [Verification step]
376	
377	---
378	
379	Each checkbox becomes a unit of work in the apply phase. Ready to implement?
380	```
381	
382	**PAUSE** - Wait for user to confirm they're ready to implement.
383	
384	Save to `openspec/changes/<name>/tasks.md`.
385	
386	---
387	
388	## Phase 9: Apply (Implementation)
389	
390	**EXPLAIN:**
391	```
392	## Implementation
393	
394	Now we implement each task, checking them off as we go. I'll announce each one and occasionally note how the specs/design informed the approach.
395	```
396	
397	**DO:** For each task:
398	
399	1. Announce: "Working on task N: [description]"
400	2. Implement the change in the codebase
401	3. Reference specs/design naturally: "The spec says X, so I'm doing Y"
402	4. Mark complete in tasks.md: `- [ ]` → `- [x]`
403	5. Brief status: "✓ Task N complete"
404	
405	Keep narration light—don't over-explain every line of code.
406	
407	After all tasks:
408	
409	```
410	## Implementation Complete
411	
412	All tasks done:
413	- [x] Task 1
414	- [x] Task 2
415	- [x] ...
416	
417	The change is implemented! One more step—let's archive it.
418	```
419	
420	---
421	
422	## Phase 10: Archive
423	
424	**EXPLAIN:**
425	```
426	## Archiving
427	
428	When a change is complete, we archive it. This moves it from `openspec/changes/` to `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/`.
429	
430	Archived changes become your project's decision history—you can always find them later to understand why something was built a certain way.
431	```
432	
433	**DO:**
434	```bash
435	openspec archive "<name>"
436	```
437	
438	**SHOW:**
439	```
440	Archived to: `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/`
441	
442	The change is now part of your project's history. The code is in your codebase, the decision record is preserved.
443	```
444	
445	---
446	
447	## Phase 11: Recap & Next Steps
448	
449	```
450	## Congratulations!
451	
452	You just completed a full OpenSpec cycle:
453	
454	1. **Explore** - Thought through the problem
455	2. **New** - Created a change container
456	3. **Proposal** - Captured WHY
457	4. **Specs** - Defined WHAT in detail
458	5. **Design** - Decided HOW
459	6. **Tasks** - Broke it into steps
460	7. **Apply** - Implemented the work
461	8. **Archive** - Preserved the record
462	
463	This same rhythm works for any size change—a small fix or a major feature.
464	
465	---
466	
467	## Command Reference
468	
469	**Core workflow:**
470	
471	 | Command           | What it does                               |
472	 |-------------------|--------------------------------------------|
473	 | `/opsx:propose` | Create a change and generate all artifacts |
474	 | `/opsx:explore` | Think through problems before/during work  |
475	 | `/opsx:apply`   | Implement tasks from a change              |
476	 | `/opsx:archive` | Archive a completed change                 |
477	
478	**Additional commands:**
479	
480	 | Command            | What it does                                             |
481	 |--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
482	 | `/opsx:new`      | Start a new change, step through artifacts one at a time |
483	 | `/opsx:continue` | Continue working on an existing change                   |
484	 | `/opsx:ff`       | Fast-forward: create all artifacts at once               |
485	 | `/opsx:verify`   | Verify implementation matches artifacts                  |
486	
487	---
488	
489	## What's Next?
490	
491	Try `/opsx:propose` on something you actually want to build. You've got the rhythm now!
492	```
493	
494	---
495	
496	## Graceful Exit Handling
497	
498	### User wants to stop mid-way
499	
500	If the user says they need to stop, want to pause, or seem disengaged:
501	
502	```
503	No problem! Your change is saved at `openspec/changes/<name>/`.
504	
505	To pick up where we left off later:
506	- `/opsx:continue <name>` - Resume artifact creation
507	- `/opsx:apply <name>` - Jump to implementation (if tasks exist)
508	
509	The work won't be lost. Come back whenever you're ready.
510	```
511	
512	Exit gracefully without pressure.
513	
514	### User just wants command reference
515	
516	If the user says they just want to see the commands or skip the tutorial:
517	
518	```
519	## OpenSpec Quick Reference
520	
521	**Core workflow:**
522	
523	 | Command                  | What it does                               |
524	 |--------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
525	 | `/opsx:propose <name>` | Create a change and generate all artifacts |
526	 | `/opsx:explore`        | Think through problems (no code changes)   |
527	 | `/opsx:apply <name>`   | Implement tasks                            |
528	 | `/opsx:archive <name>` | Archive when done                          |
529	
530	**Additional commands:**
531	
532	 | Command                   | What it does                        |
533	 |---------------------------|-------------------------------------|
534	 | `/opsx:new <name>`      | Start a new change, step by step    |
535	 | `/opsx:continue <name>` | Continue an existing change         |
536	 | `/opsx:ff <name>`       | Fast-forward: all artifacts at once |
537	 | `/opsx:verify <name>`   | Verify implementation               |
538	
539	Try `/opsx:propose` to start your first change.
540	```
541	
542	Exit gracefully.
543	
544	---
545	
546	## Guardrails
547	
548	- **Follow the EXPLAIN → DO → SHOW → PAUSE pattern** at key transitions (after explore, after proposal draft, after tasks, after archive)
549	- **Keep narration light** during implementation—teach without lecturing
550	- **Don't skip phases** even if the change is small—the goal is teaching the workflow
551	- **Pause for acknowledgment** at marked points, but don't over-pause
552	- **Handle exits gracefully**—never pressure the user to continue
553	- **Use real codebase tasks**—don't simulate or use fake examples
554	- **Adjust scope gently**—guide toward smaller tasks but respect user choice
555

1	## ADDED Requirements
2	
3	### Requirement: OpenSpec graph source binding
4	
5	系统 SHALL 为 OpenSpec graph 记录其细图数据来源绑定。
6	
7	#### Scenario: Dataset task binding
8	- **WHEN** graph sync receives a dataset id and task id
9	- **THEN** graph metadata SHALL record `source_kind` as `dataset_task`
10	- **AND** graph metadata SHALL record the dataset id and task id
11	- **AND** Event Graph SHALL be built from the Dataset task trace
12	
13	#### Scenario: Session task binding
14	- **WHEN** graph sync receives a session id and task id
15	- **THEN** graph metadata SHALL record `source_kind` as `session_task`
16	- **AND** Event Graph SHALL be built from normalized session events within that task boundary
17	
18	#### Scenario: Session full binding
19	- **WHEN** graph sync receives a session id without a task id
20	- **THEN** graph metadata SHALL record `source_kind` as `session_full`
21	- **AND** Event Graph SHALL be built from normalized session events
22	- **AND** diagnosis SHALL mark confidence lower than task-scoped evidence
23	
24	#### Scenario: Missing step evidence
25	- **WHEN** graph sync cannot resolve Dataset or session step evidence
26	- **THEN** graph metadata SHALL record `source_kind` as `milestone_fallback`
27	- **AND** diagnosis SHALL include `missing_evidence` explaining that session step evidence is unavailable
28	
29	### Requirement: Step-level Event Graph for OpenSpec graph
30	
31	OpenSpec graph sync SHALL use session step evidence as the primary Event Graph source.
32	
33	#### Scenario: Step events become graph nodes
34	- **WHEN** normalized session events contain user messages, assistant text, tool calls, tool results, commands, file edits, errors, or final claims
35	- **THEN** Event Graph SHALL create nodes for those step events

2	
3	### Requirement: OpenSpec graph source binding
4	
5	系统 SHALL 为 OpenSpec graph 记录其细图数据来源绑定。
6	
7	#### Scenario: Dataset task binding
8	- **WHEN** graph sync receives a dataset id and task id
9	- **THEN** graph metadata SHALL record `source_kind` as `dataset_task`
10	- **AND** graph metadata SHALL record the dataset id and task id
11	- **AND** Event Graph SHALL be built from the Dataset task trace
12	
13	#### Scenario: Session task binding
14	- **WHEN** graph sync receives a session id and task id
15	- **THEN** graph metadata SHALL record `source_kind` as `session_task`
16	- **AND** Event Graph SHALL be built from normalized session events within that task boundary
17	
18	#### Scenario: Session full binding
19	- **WHEN** graph sync receives a session id without a task id
20	- **THEN** graph metadata SHALL record `source_kind` as `session_full`
21	- **AND** Event Graph SHALL be built from normalized session events
22	- **AND** diagnosis SHALL mark confidence lower than task-scoped evidence
23	
24	#### Scenario: Missing step evidence
25	- **WHEN** graph sync cannot resolve Dataset or session step evidence
26	- **THEN** graph metadata SHALL record `source_kind` as `milestone_fallback`
27	- **AND** diagnosis SHALL include `missing_evidence` explaining that session step evidence is unavailable
28	
29	### Requirement: Step-level Event Graph for OpenSpec graph
30	
31	OpenSpec graph sync SHALL use session step evidence as the primary Event Graph source.
32	
33	#### Scenario: Step events become graph nodes
34	- **WHEN** normalized session events contain user messages, assistant text, tool calls, tool results, commands, file edits, errors, or final claims
35	- **THEN** Event Graph SHALL create nodes for those step events
36	- **AND** each node SHALL preserve event id, event type, timestamp, agent id, turn index, summary, and raw evidence reference when available
37	
38	#### Scenario: Tool and file details are preserved
39	- **WHEN** a step event contains tool name, tool call id, command, or file paths
40	- **THEN** Event Graph node data SHALL preserve those fields for mapping and Viewer inspection
41	
42	#### Scenario: Milestones are supplemental
43	- **WHEN** `graph/events.jsonl` contains milestone events and session step evidence is available
44	- **THEN** milestone events SHALL be stored as supplemental evidence or graph metadata
45	- **AND** milestone events SHALL NOT replace the step-level Event Graph main nodes
46	
47	### Requirement: Action mapping reasons
48	
49	系统 SHALL explain why each Event maps to each OpenSpec Action.
50	
51	#### Scenario: Mapping reason output
52	- **WHEN** an Event is mapped to an Action
53	- **THEN** Action evidence SHALL include the mapped event id
54	- **AND** Action evidence SHALL include a reason such as `path:proposal`, `path:spec`, `path:design`, `path:tasks`, `command:openspec_validate`, `command:test`, `command:openspec_archive`, `event:file_change`, or `unmapped_turn`
55	
56	#### Scenario: Unmapped step retention
57	- **WHEN** a step event cannot be mapped to a fixed OpenSpec Action
58	- **THEN** Event Graph SHALL retain the event
59	- **AND** mapping SHALL mark it as unmapped or ad hoc evidence instead of dropping it

1	"""Backward attribution over OpenSpec Action Graphs."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from collections import defaultdict, deque
6	
7	from .models import ActionGraph, CausalChain, Symptom
8	
9	
10	EVIDENCE_POINTS = {"high": 20, "medium": 12, "low": 5}
11	ROOT_CAUSE_LABELS = {
12	    "missing_required_action": "OpenSpec required action is missing",
13	    "unsupported_final_claim": "Final claim is not supported by workflow evidence",
14	    "validation_failed": "Validation failed",
15	    "workflow_skip": "Workflow skipped a required upstream action",
16	    "artifact_missing_or_empty": "Required OpenSpec artifact evidence is missing",
17	}
18	
19	
20	def attribute_symptoms(action_graph: ActionGraph, symptoms: list[Symptom]) -> list[CausalChain]:
21	    actions = {action.action_id: action for action in action_graph.actions}
22	    reverse_edges = defaultdict(list)
23	    forward_edges = defaultdict(list)
24	    for edge in action_graph.edges:
25	        reverse_edges[edge.to_id].append(edge.from_id)
26	        forward_edges[edge.from_id].append(edge.to_id)
27	
28	    chains: list[CausalChain] = []
29	    best_scores: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
30	    for symptom in symptoms:
31	        candidates = _upstream_distances(symptom.action_id, reverse_edges)
32	        if symptom.action_id not in candidates:
33	            candidates[symptom.action_id] = 0
34	        for action_id, distance in candidates.items():
35	            action = actions.get(action_id)
36	            if not action:
37	                continue
38	            score = _score_candidate(symptom, action_id, distance, action_graph, forward_edges)
39	            best_scores[action_id] = max(best_scores[action_id], score)
40	            chains.append(
41	                CausalChain(
42	                    root_action_id=action_id,
43	                    root_cause=_root_cause(symptom.type, action.type),
44	                    score=score,
45	                    confidence=_confidence(score),
46	                    chain=_chain_to_symptom(action_id, symptom, reverse_edges),
47	                    evidence=[*symptom.evidence, *_action_evidence_text(action)],
48	                )
49	            )
50	
51	    for action in action_graph.actions:
52	        action.suspicion_score = int(best_scores.get(action.action_id, 0))
53	
54	    chains.sort(key=lambda chain: chain.score, reverse=True)
55	    return chains[:10]
56	
57	
58	def _upstream_distances(start: str, reverse_edges: dict[str, list[str]]) -> dict[str, int]:
59	    result: dict[str, int] = {}
60	    queue = deque([(start, 0)])
61	    while queue:
62	        current, distance = queue.popleft()
63	        for parent in reverse_edges.get(current, []):
64	            if parent in result:
65	                continue
66	            result[parent] = distance + 1
67	            queue.append((parent, distance + 1))
68	    return result
69	
70	
71	def _score_candidate(
72	    symptom: Symptom,
73	    action_id: str,
74	    distance: int,
75	    action_graph: ActionGraph,
76	    forward_edges: dict[str, list[str]],
77	) -> int:
78	    actions = {action.action_id: action for action in action_graph.actions}
79	    action = actions[action_id]
80	    score = 0
81	    if symptom.type in {"missing_required_action", "artifact_missing_or_empty", "unsupported_final_claim"} or action.status in {"missing", "skipped"}:
82	        score += 40
83	    score += max(0, 25 - max(0, distance - 1) * 5)
84	    score += _evidence_points(action)
85	    if _template_index(action_id, action_graph) <= _template_index(symptom.action_id, action_graph):
86	        score += 10
87	    score += min(5, _downstream_count(action_id, forward_edges))
88	    return max(0, min(100, score))
89	
90	
91	def _evidence_points(action) -> int:
92	    if action.status in {"missing", "skipped"}:
93	        return 20
94	    best = 0
95	    for item in action.evidence:
96	        if isinstance(item, dict):
97	            best = max(best, EVIDENCE_POINTS.get(str(item.get("confidence")), 0))
98	    return best or 5
99	
100	
101	def _template_index(action_id: str, action_graph: ActionGraph) -> int:
102	    for index, action in enumerate(action_graph.actions):
103	        if action.action_id == action_id:
104	            return index
105	    return 999
106	
107	
108	def _downstream_count(action_id: str, forward_edges: dict[str, list[str]]) -> int:
109	    seen: set[str] = set()
110	    queue = deque([action_id])
111	    while queue:
112	        current = queue.popleft()
113	        for child in forward_edges.get(current, []):
114	            if child in seen:
115	                continue
116	            seen.add(child)
117	            queue.append(child)
118	    return len(seen)
119	
120	
121	def _confidence(score: int) -> str:
122	    if score >= 80:
123	        return "high"
124	    if score >= 50:
125	        return "medium"
126	    return "low"
127	
128	
129	def _root_cause(symptom_type: str, action_type: str) -> str:
130	    return f"{ROOT_CAUSE_LABELS.get(symptom_type, symptom_type)}: {action_type}"
131	
132	
133	def _chain_to_symptom(action_id: str, symptom: Symptom, reverse_edges: dict[str, list[str]]) -> list[str]:
134	    if action_id == symptom.action_id:
135	        return [action_id, symptom.symptom_id]
136	    parents = {child: parent for child, items in reverse_edges.items() for parent in items}
137	    path = [symptom.action_id]
138	    current = symptom.action_id
139	    while current != action_id and current in parents:
140	        current = parents[current]
141	        path.append(current)
142	    path.reverse()
143	    path.append(symptom.symptom_id)
144	    return path
145	
146	
147	def _action_evidence_text(action) -> list[str]:
148	    result = []
149	    if action.event_ids:
150	        result.append(f"{action.action_id} mapped events: {', '.join(action.event_ids)}")
151	    if action.expected_because:
152	        result.append(f"{action.action_id} expected because: {', '.join(action.expected_because)}")
153	    return result
154

2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import shutil
6	import subprocess
7	import time
8	from pathlib import Path
9	from typing import Any
10	
11	
12	ANALYZE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120
13	
14	
15	class AnalysisError(Exception):
16	    """User-facing analysis failure."""
17	
18	    def __init__(self, message: str, code: str = "analysis_error") -> None:
19	        super().__init__(message)
20	        self.message = message
21	        self.code = code
22

24	import os as _os
25	
26	from ccwhat.analyzers.registry import get as _get_analyzer_spec, list_names as _list_analyzer_names
27	
28	_KNOWN_BINARY_PATHS = {
29	    "codex": "/Applications/Codex.app/Contents/Resources/codex",
30	    "opencode": "/Applications/OpenCode.app/Contents/MacOS/opencode",
31	}
32	
33	
34	def _resolve_binary(cmd: list[str]) -> list[str]:
35	    if not cmd:
36	        return cmd
37	    binary = cmd[0]
38	    if Path(binary).is_file():
39	        return cmd
40	    resolved = shutil.which(binary)
41	    if resolved:
42	        updated = list(cmd)
43	        updated[0] = resolved
44	        return updated
45	    known = _KNOWN_BINARY_PATHS.get(binary)
46	    if known and Path(known).is_file():
47	        updated = list(cmd)
48	        updated[0] = known
49	        return updated
50	    return cmd
51	
52	
53	def _normalize_analyzer_agent(agent: str | None) -> str:
54	    from ccwhat.analyzers.registry import _normalize
55	    return _normalize(agent or "claude")
56	
57	
58	def _default_analyze_cmd(agent: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
59	    normalized = _normalize_analyzer_agent(agent)
60	    spec = _get_analyzer_spec(normalized)
61	    if spec is None:
62	        raise AnalysisError(
63	            f"Analyzer protocol is not supported for agent '{normalized}'. "
64	            f"Supported agents: {', '.join(_list_analyzer_names())}",
65	            "analyzer_not_supported",
66	        )
67	    return list(spec.default_command)
68	
69	
70	def _analyze_cmd(
71	    cmd: list[str] | tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
72	    agent: str | None = None,
73	) -> list[str]:
74	    if cmd:
75	        return _resolve_binary(list(cmd))
76	    raw = _os.environ.get("CCWHAT_ANALYZE_CMD", "").strip()
77	    if raw:
78	        import shlex
79	        return _resolve_binary(shlex.split(raw))
80	    return _resolve_binary(_default_analyze_cmd(agent))
81	
82	
83	def _analyze_spec(
84	    cmd: list[str] | tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
85	    agent: str | None = None,
86	) -> tuple[Any, list[str]]:
87	    """Return (spec_or_None, resolved_command) for the given config."""
88	    normalized = _normalize_analyzer_agent(agent)
89	    env_cmd = _os.environ.get("CCWHAT_ANALYZE_CMD", "").strip()
90	    # Only use the analyzer spec when neither explicit cmd nor env override is provided
91	    spec = _get_analyzer_spec(normalized) if (not cmd and not env_cmd) else None
92	    resolved_cmd = _analyze_cmd(cmd, agent=agent)
93	    return spec, resolved_cmd
94	
95	
96	def _resolve_analyzer_agent(
97	    agent: str | None = None,
98	    *,
99	    default_agent: str | None = None,
100	) -> str:
101	    """Resolve the analyzer agent name.
102	
103	    Priority:
104	    1. Explicit ``agent`` parameter
105	    2. CCWHAT_ANALYZE_AGENT env var
106	    3. ``default_agent`` (adapter name / session agent)
107	    4. ``"claude"`` fallback
108	    """
109	    if agent:
110	        return _normalize_analyzer_agent(agent)
111	    env_agent = _os.environ.get("CCWHAT_ANALYZE_AGENT", "").strip()
112	    if env_agent:
113	        return _normalize_analyzer_agent(env_agent)
114	    if default_agent:
115	        return _normalize_analyzer_agent(default_agent)
116	    return "claude"
117	
118	
119	def _resolve_analyzer_timeout(timeout: int | None = None, spec: Any = None) -> int:
120	    """Resolve timeout from explicit param, env var, spec default, or global default.
121	
122	    Priority:
123	    1. Explicit ``timeout`` parameter
124	    2. CCWHAT_ANALYZE_TIMEOUT env var
125	    3. ``spec.timeout_seconds``
126	    4. ``ANALYZE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`` (120)
127	    """
128	    if timeout is not None and timeout > 0:
129	        return timeout
130	    env_timeout = _os.environ.get("CCWHAT_ANALYZE_TIMEOUT", "").strip()
131	    if env_timeout:
132	        try:
133	            parsed = int(env_timeout)
134	            if parsed > 0:
135	                return parsed
136	        except ValueError:
137	            pass
138	    if spec is not None and getattr(spec, "timeout_seconds", None) and spec.timeout_seconds > 0:
139	        return spec.timeout_seconds
140	    return ANALYZE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
141	
142	
143	def _run_one_try(
144	    prompt: str,
145	    cmd_list: list[str],
146	    timeout_sec: int,
147	    spec: Any,
148	    runner: Any,
149	    extra_files: dict[str, str] | None = None,
150	) -> tuple[str, int]:
151	    """Run a single analyzer attempt and return (report, elapsed_ms) or raise AnalysisError."""
152	    started = time.monotonic()
153	    resolved = _resolve_binary(cmd_list)
154	    try:
155	        result = runner(
156	            resolved,
157	            input=prompt,
158	            capture_output=True,
159	            text=True,
160	            timeout=timeout_sec,
161	        )
162	    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
163	        raise AnalysisError(
164	            f"Analyzer command not found: {resolved[0]!r}.\n"
165	            "Set CCWHAT_ANALYZE_CMD to your AI CLI command, e.g.:\n"
166	            "  export CCWHAT_ANALYZE_CMD='claude -p -'",
167	            "analyzer_not_found",
168	        ) from exc
169	    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
170	        raise AnalysisError(f"Analysis timed out after {timeout_sec} seconds.", "analyzer_timeout") from exc
171	
172	    elapsed_ms = int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)
173	    stdout = (result.stdout or "").strip()
174	    stderr = (result.stderr or "").strip()
175	
176	    if result.returncode != 0:
177	        detail = stderr or stdout or f"exit code {result.returncode}"
178	        raise AnalysisError(f"Analysis failed: {detail}", "analyzer_failed")
179	
180	    if not stdout and spec and spec.output_mode == "stdout":
181	        detail = stderr or f"{resolved[0]} returned empty output"
182	        raise AnalysisError(f"Analysis produced no report: {detail}", "empty_report")
183	
184	    if spec and spec.output_mode != "stdout" and spec.parse_output:
185	        try:
186	            parsed = spec.parse_output(stdout, stderr, extra_files or {})
187	            if not parsed.strip():
188	                if not stdout.strip():
189	                    detail = stderr or f"{resolved[0]} returned empty output"
190	                    raise AnalysisError(
191	                        f"Analysis produced no report: {detail}",
192	                        "empty_report",
193	                    )
194	                raise AnalysisError(
195	                    "Analyzer output parser produced empty report. "
196	                    "The command may have returned an unexpected format.",
197	                    "analyzer_output_parse_error",
198	                )
199	            return parsed, elapsed_ms
200	        except AnalysisError:
201	            raise
202	        except Exception as exc:
203	            raise AnalysisError(
204	                f"Failed to parse analyzer output: {exc}",
205	                "analyzer_output_parse_error",
206	            ) from exc
207	
208	    return stdout, elapsed_ms
209	
210	
211	def run_mc_analysis(
212	    prompt: str,
213	    timeout: int | None = None,
214	    runner: Any | None = None,
215	    cmd: list[str] | tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
216	    agent: str | None = None,
217	    default_agent: str | None = None,
218	) -> tuple[str, int]:
219	    from ccwhat.analyzers.registry import (
220	        get_candidates,
221	        prepare_candidate,
222	    )
223	
224	    normalized_agent = _resolve_analyzer_agent(agent, default_agent=default_agent)
225	    spec, resolved_cmd = _analyze_spec(cmd, agent=normalized_agent)
226	    effective_timeout = _resolve_analyzer_timeout(timeout, spec=spec)
227	    env_cmd = _os.environ.get("CCWHAT_ANALYZE_CMD", "").strip()
228	
229	    has_cmd_source = bool(cmd) or bool(env_cmd)
230	
231	    # If explicit cmd or env override, use it directly (no fallback)
232	    if has_cmd_source:
233	        run = runner or subprocess.run
234	        return _run_one_try(prompt, resolved_cmd, effective_timeout, spec, run)
235	
236	    # No explicit cmd — use the primary spec
237	    if spec is None:
238	        raise AnalysisError(
239	            f"Analyzer protocol is not supported for agent '{normalized_agent}'. "
240	            f"Supported agents: {', '.join(_list_analyzer_names())}",
241	            "analyzer_not_supported",
242	        )
243	
244	    run = runner or subprocess.run
245	    candidates = get_candidates(normalized_agent)
246	    if not candidates:
247	        # No fallback candidates — try the primary spec once
248	        return _run_one_try(prompt, resolved_cmd, effective_timeout, spec, run)
249	
250	    # Try primary spec first, then fallback candidates
251	    last_error: AnalysisError | None = None
252	    try:
253	        return _run_one_try(prompt, resolved_cmd, effective_timeout, spec, run)
254	    except (AnalysisError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as primary_err:
255	        cmd_not_found = isinstance(primary_err, AnalysisError) and primary_err.code == "analyzer_not_found"
256	        if cmd_not_found:
257	            raise
258	        last_error = _as_analysis_error(primary_err, effective_timeout)
259	
260	    # Try fallback candidates
261	    _cleanup_dirs: list[str] = []
262	    try:
263	        for candidate in candidates:
264	            try:
265	                cand_cmd, extra = prepare_candidate(candidate)
266	                _cleanup_dirs.append(str(Path(extra.get("last_message_file", "")).parent))
267	                candidate_timeout = _resolve_analyzer_timeout(timeout, spec=candidate)
268	                result = _run_one_try(prompt, cand_cmd, candidate_timeout, candidate, run, extra_files=extra)
269	                return result
270	            except (AnalysisError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as fallback_err:
271	                fnf = isinstance(fallback_err, AnalysisError) and fallback_err.code == "analyzer_not_found"
272	                if fnf:
273	                    raise
274	                candidate_timeout = _resolve_analyzer_timeout(timeout, spec=candidate)
275	                last_error = _as_analysis_error(fallback_err, candidate_timeout)
276	                continue
277	    finally:
278	        for d in _cleanup_dirs:
279	            if d and Path(d).is_dir():
280	                import shutil as _su
281	                try:
282	                    _su.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
283	                except Exception:
284	                    pass
285	
286	    if last_error:
287	        raise AnalysisError(
288	            f"{last_error.message}\n\n"
289	            f"Analyzer agent: {normalized_agent} (experimental={spec.experimental}). "
290	            f"Timeout: {effective_timeout}s. "
291	            f"Fallback tried: {len(candidates)} candidate(s). "
292	            f"Try setting CCWHAT_ANALYZE_TIMEOUT to a larger value or "
293	            f"CCWHAT_ANALYZE_AGENT=claude to use the stable analyzer.",
294	            code=last_error.code,
295	        )
296	    raise AnalysisError(
297	        f"All analyzer attempts failed for agent '{normalized_agent}'.",
298	        "analyzer_failed",
299	    )
300	
301	
302	def _as_analysis_error(exc: Exception, timeout_sec: int) -> AnalysisError:
303	    if isinstance(exc, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
304	        return AnalysisError(f"Analysis timed out after {timeout_sec} seconds.", "analyzer_timeout")
305	    if isinstance(exc, AnalysisError):
306	        return exc
307	    return AnalysisError(str(exc), "analyzer_failed")

Here is a thorough report of all findings.

---

## 1. OpenSpec Workflow Structure

### Directory Layout

The OpenSpec-related files live in three key locations:

- **`/Users/elon2ge/workspace/CCWhat/openspec/`** -- The main OpenSpec directory
  - `config.yaml` -- Project config (schema: spec-driven, rules for artifact languages)
  - `changes/` -- Active changes (not yet archived)
  - `changes/archive/` -- Past completed changes (dated archives)
  - `specs/` -- Canonical specs for various capabilities

- **`/Users/elon2ge/workspace/CCWhat/.claude/skills/openspec-*`** -- Claude Code skill definitions for the workflow
  - `openspec-propose/SKILL.md` -- Create a new change with all artifacts
  - `openspec-explore/SKILL.md` -- Think through problems before implementing
  - `openspec-apply-change/SKILL.md` -- Implement tasks from a change
  - `openspec-archive-change/SKILL.md` -- Archive a completed change
  - `openspec-onboard/SKILL.md` -- Guided onboarding walkthrough

- **`/Users/elon2ge/workspace/CCWhat/.claude/commands/opsx/*`** -- Slash command definitions for OPSX (early name for OpenSpec)
  - `/opsx:propose`, `/opsx:apply`, `/opsx:archive`, `/opsx:explore`, `/opsx:onboard`

### The OpenSpec Workflow Cycle

The artifact creation order for a `spec-driven` schema change:

1. **proposal.md** -- "Why" and "What Changes" at high level, non-goals
2. **design.md** -- "How": context, decisions, tradeoffs, risks
3. **specs/`<capability>`/spec.md** -- "What" in precise requirement/scenario format (WHEN/THEN/AND)
4. **tasks.md** -- Implementation checklist with numbered `- [ ]` checkbox items grouped by category
5. Apply phase -- Check off tasks, implement code
6. Archive -- Move to `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/`

The CLI tools involved: `openspec new change`, `openspec status --json`, `openspec instructions`, `ccwhat openspec-graph sync`.

### Current Active Changes

Two changes are listed as "complete" but neither is archived:

- **`add-symptom-routed-graph-attribution`** -- 24/24 tasks complete
- **`round-viewer-action-buttons`** -- 5/5 tasks complete

(There is no `.openspec/` directory at the project root -- the dot-prefix variant was renamed to `openspec/`.)

---

## 2. File: `ccwhat/diagnosis/feedback.py` (Full Content)

**Path:** `/Users/elon2ge/workspace/CCWhat/ccwhat/diagnosis/feedback.py`

This file contains **302 lines** with the following functions and constants:

### Constants
- `MAX_GRAPH_CONTEXT_CHARS = 28_000`
- `MAX_TEXT_PREVIEW = 700`
- `MAX_TOOL_INPUT_PREVIEW = 900`

### Public Functions

**`analyze_graph_feedback(feedback, action_graph, event_graph, analyzer_cmd, analyzer_agent, analyzer_timeout, runner)`** (lines 18-49)
- Orchestrates the full diagnosis flow: builds a prompt, calls `run_mc_analysis()`, parses the output, validates it, and returns a structured result with elapsed time.

**`build_graph_attribution_prompt(feedback, action_graph, event_graph)`** (lines 52-59)
- Reads the asset template `ccwhat/assets/graph_attribution_prompt.md` and fills in `{{feedback}}` and `{{graph_context}}`.

**`build_compact_graph_context(action_graph, event_graph)`** (lines 62-108)
- Selects the most important events by priority (errors first, then file_edit, command, etc.), compacting them, and returns a JSON string with compact actions and events. Up to `MAX_GRAPH_CONTEXT_CHARS` total.

**`parse_graph_attribution_output(raw)`** (lines 111-130)
- Parses the raw analyzer output: strips Markdown code fences if present, tries `json.loads()`, falls back to `JSONDecoder.raw_decode()`. Validates the result is a `dict`.

**`validate_graph_attribution_result(value, action_graph, event_graph)`** (lines 133-217)
- Validates all Action/Event references from the analyzer output against the real graphs. Removes fabricated IDs, corrects event-to-action mapping mismatches, deduplicates, clips text to limits. Returns a structured result with `available`, `status`, `symptoms`, `suspicious_actions`, `suspicious_events`, `missing_evidence`, `summary`.

### Private Helpers
- `_compact_event(node)` (lines 220-238) -- Extracts key fields for JSON compacting
- `_event_priority(node)` (lines 241-254) -- Priority scoring: error=100, file_edit=90, etc.
- `_unavailable_result(code, message)` (lines 257-267) -- Structured error result
- `_dict_list(value)` (line 270) -- Safe cast to list of dicts
- `_string_list(value)` (line 274) -- Safe cast to list of strings
- `_clip(value, limit)` (lines 278-284) -- Truncate text with ellipsis
- `_clip_json(value, limit)` (lines 287-291) -- Truncate JSON with ellipsis
- `_dedupe(values)` (lines 294-301) -- Deduplicate a string list while preserving order

---

## 3. Test File: `test_graph_feedback.py`

**Path:** `/Users/elon2ge/workspace/CCWhat/tests/test_graph_feedback.py` (130 lines)

This file imports four functions from `ccwhat.diagnosis.feedback`:
- `analyze_graph_feedback`
- `build_compact_graph_context`
- `parse_graph_attribution_output`
- `validate_graph_attribution_result`

### Test Data
- `ACTION_GRAPH` with two actions: A5 (apply, observed, event_ids=["E40"]) and A6 (verify, failed, event_ids=["E41"])
- `EVENT_GRAPH` with two nodes: E40 (file_edit, wrong content) and E41 (tool_result, FAILED routing test)

### Test Cases (class `GraphFeedbackTests`)
1. **`test_compact_context_keeps_graph_ids_and_tool_evidence`** -- Verifies the compacted context preserves event_ids and tool_input fields.
2. **`test_parse_accepts_markdown_json_fence`** -- Verifies `parse_graph_attribution_output` strips Markdown code fences.
3. **`test_validate_removes_fabricated_ids_and_corrects_mapping`** -- Verifies fabricated Action A99 and Event E999 are stripped, event-to-action mapping is corrected when mismatched, and original valid IDs are preserved.
4. **`test_analyze_reuses_local_analyzer_runner_once`** -- Verifies the analyzer is called exactly once with correct command and input, and results flow through.
5. **`test_analyzer_failure_returns_structured_unavailable_result`** -- Verifies that a `FileNotFoundError` from the runner results in `available=False` and `code="analyzer_not_found"`.

---

## 4. Function `parse_graph_attribution_output`

**Location:** `/Users/elon2ge/workspace/CCWhat/ccwhat/diagnosis/feedback.py`, lines 111-130

```python
def parse_graph_attribution_output(raw: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
```

This function:
1. Strips and validates input is non-empty
2. Tries to match a Markdown fenced JSON block (`` ```json ... ``` `` or `` ``` ... ``` ``)
3. Falls back to treating the full text as JSON
4. On `json.JSONDecodeError`, tries to find the first `{` and use `JSONDecoder.raw_decode()`
5. Validates the result is a `dict`, otherwise raises `ValueError`

---

## 5. Function `validate_graph_attribution_result`

**Location:** `/Users/elon2ge/workspace/CCWhat/ccwhat/diagnosis/feedback.py`, lines 133-217

```python
def validate_graph_attribution_result(
    value: dict[str, Any],
    action_graph: dict[str, Any],
    event_graph: dict[str, Any],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
```

This function:
1. Builds lookup maps from `action_graph["actions"]` (by `action_id`) and `event_graph["nodes"]` (by `node_id`)
2. Builds reverse map of `event_id -> [action_ids]`
3. Validates `suspicious_actions` -- filters out unknown Action IDs, adds them to `missing_evidence`
4. Validates `suspicious_events` -- filters out unknown Event IDs, corrects event-to-action mapping when the analyzer's claimed action is not among the actual mapped actions
5. Collects up to 6 `symptoms` and clips their fields
6. Sets `status` to `"complete"` if any suspicious actions or events remain, otherwise `"insufficient_evidence"`
7. Returns `{"available": True, "status", "symptoms", "suspicious_actions", "suspicious_events", "missing_evidence", "summary"}`

---

## 6. Existing OpenSpec Change: `add-symptom-routed-graph-attribution`

This is the active reference change, located at `/Users/elon2ge/workspace/CCWhat/openspec/changes/add-symptom-routed-graph-attribution/`. All 24 tasks are marked complete.

32	            prompt,

37	        )

52	def build_graph_attribution_prompt(
53	    feedback: str,
54	    action_graph: dict[str, Any],
55	    event_graph: dict[str, Any],
56	) -> str:
57	    template = resources.files("ccwhat").joinpath("assets/graph_attribution_prompt.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
58	    context = build_compact_graph_context(action_graph, event_graph)
59	    return template.replace("{{feedback}}", feedback.strip()).replace("{{graph_context}}", context)

62	def build_compact_graph_context(
63	    action_graph: dict[str, Any],
64	    event_graph: dict[str, Any],
65	) -> str:
66	    actions = [item for item in action_graph.get("actions", []) if isinstance(item, dict)]
67	    nodes = [item for item in event_graph.get("nodes", []) if isinstance(item, dict)]
68	
69	    ranked = sorted(enumerate(nodes), key=lambda item: (-_event_priority(item[1]), item[0]))
70	    selected_indexes: set[int] = set()
71	    used = 0
72	    compact_by_index: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
73	    for index, node in ranked:
74	        compact = _compact_event(node)
75	        size = len(json.dumps(compact, ensure_ascii=False))
76	        if used + size > MAX_GRAPH_CONTEXT_CHARS and selected_indexes:
77	            continue
78	        selected_indexes.add(index)
79	        compact_by_index[index] = compact
80	        used += size
81	
82	    selected_events = [compact_by_index[index] for index in sorted(selected_indexes)]
83	    selected_ids = {str(item.get("event_id") or "") for item in selected_events}
84	    compact_actions = []
85	    for action in actions:
86	        event_ids = [str(value) for value in action.get("event_ids", []) if str(value) in selected_ids]
87	        compact_actions.append({
88	            "action_id": action.get("action_id"),
89	            "type": action.get("type"),
90	            "status": action.get("status"),
91	            "event_ids": event_ids,
92	            "mapping_reasons": [
93	                item.get("reason")
94	                for item in action.get("evidence", [])
95	                if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("reason")
96	            ][:12],
97	        })
98	
99	    return json.dumps(
100	        {
101	            "actions": compact_actions,
102	            "events": selected_events,
103	            "omitted_event_count": max(0, len(nodes) - len(selected_events)),
104	            "source_note": "Claude Code raw Session behavior; final repository state is not verified",
105	        },
106	        ensure_ascii=False,
107	        indent=2,
108	    )

111	def parse_graph_attribution_output(raw: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
112	    text = str(raw or "").strip()
113	    if not text:
114	        raise ValueError("Analyzer returned empty diagnosis output.")
115	
116	    fenced = re.search(r"```(?:json)?\s*(\{.*?\})\s*```", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
117	    candidate = fenced.group(1) if fenced else text
118	    try:
119	        value = json.loads(candidate)
120	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
121	        start = candidate.find("{")
122	        if start < 0:
123	            raise ValueError("Analyzer output does not contain a JSON object.") from None
124	        try:
125	            value, _ = json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(candidate[start:])
126	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
127	            raise ValueError(f"Analyzer output is not valid diagnosis JSON: {exc.msg}.") from exc
128	    if not isinstance(value, dict):
129	        raise ValueError("Analyzer diagnosis JSON must be an object.")
130	    return value
